probes.line: Word is a rival's circling something similar. Why yours?
Walk me through the money. What does this actually make?
How fast can this be in theaters?

positions.line: Let's do it. Full price, straight to script.
Draft-first deal. Half now, half if I like page thirty.
It's not for us. But keep bringing me the weird ones.
I'd rather greenlight a documentary about this meeting.

accept: {writer} tries to play it cool and fails beautifully.
{writer} shakes your hand with both hands, then a third time.
counter: {writer} squints. 'Half now... and a producer credit for my mother.'
{writer} exhales through their nose for a full six seconds.
walk: {writer} closes the folder with terrible gentleness. 'Pinnacle returns my calls.'

casting.title: Casting Interview
opens: {cast} arrives {lateness} minutes late, in character as someone punctual.
{cast} enters, compliments the room, sits in your chair.
asks: I don't do mornings. Mornings are for people whose faces bounce back.
My rate went up. My last movie? We don't discuss it, and that costs extra.
I want this part. I want it the way I want the rider honored: completely.

plays.line: Full rate. The rider too. Even the weird parts.
Sixty-five percent — but top billing and the poster's good side.
Scale now, points on the back end. Bet on yourself.
You were the best thing in {flatterTitle} and you know it.

accept: A slow smile. 'When do we shoot?'
'Finally. Someone with taste and a checkbook.'
acceptGrudge: 'Fine. But I'm remembering this number.' She will.
'Done. My agent will cry, which I enjoy.'
demand: 'The number AND the rider. The parrot is non-negotiable.'
walk: 'Call Pinnacle. Oh wait — they called me.' Exit, perfect posture.

defenses.line: Look at the trend line, not the headline. The slate's working.
That one's on me. It won't happen twice.
The director went forty shots over. Direct your questions there.

victories.line: The team delivered. I just kept the lights on and the egos apart.
Read the number again. Slowly. I'll wait.
Imagine what that number looks like if you loosen the purse strings.

satisfied: Nods around the table. One member takes a second pastry: the highest honor.
'Continue.' From this board, that's a parade.
neutral: Pens click. Notes are made. The notes are about you.
'Noted.' The word hangs there like weather.
displeased: Someone underlines something twice. You can hear it.
The chairman looks at his watch, which is engraved with your predecessor's initials.

problems.behind: We're {days} days behind. The director calls it 'finding the film.' I call it {cost}.
problems.over: Burn rate's up {pct}%. The {department} budget is now performance art.
problems.friction: {cast} and the director communicate exclusively through a PA named Dev. Dev is 22. Dev is breaking.
problems.scope: The director wants {shots} more VFX shots. The phrase 'trust me' was used {trust} times.

plays.line: Give them what they need. Quality is the receipt.
The answer is the schedule. The schedule is the answer.
Half. And I want it in writing that half is generous.
Remind everyone that 'wrapped early' is also a career highlight.

good: The director salutes with a rolled-up shot list.
bad: Somewhere, a trailer door closes with intent.
The set gets very quiet, then very expensive.

reveals.line: Title and logo tease. Leave them hungry.
Bring out the star. Let the room lose its mind.

answers.line: Canon. All of it. Yes to everything.

awards.title: Awards Ceremony

tableTalk.line: Win or lose, you made something real. Also please don't check your phone during the montage.
If you win tonight, I'm greenlighting the sequel from this chair.
To the movie — and to whoever finds my seat filler a drink.

winLines: The room stands. Your table screams. The orchestra tries to play someone off and fails.
Confetti. Tears. Someone thanks a parrot.
loseLines: Polite applause. Your nominee's smile could cut glass.
The camera finds your table at the exact wrong moment.

plays.line: Give me until {deadline}. I'll have it fixed or framed.
The board hired a gambler. This is what the middle of a bet looks like.
Have I mentioned that tie is board-quality? Sit. Coffee?

good: 'I'll hold you to it.' They write the date on a cuff.
A grunt that, in executive, means hope.
neutral: 'Hm.' The exec pockets a desk mint on the way out.
'The board reads the trades, you know.' They know.
bad: 'I'll soften it for the board. This week.'
The door closes at a volume with a message in it.

carpetLines.line: "It's the team's night. I just signed the checks."
"This is the best picture this studio has ever made. Print it."
"Ask me again after the third act."

toasts.line: Toast the star — tonight their name is above yours.
Toast the director — they bled for every frame.
Toast the room — nobody remembers who paid. Remind no one.

plays.line: Order for them. Compliment the last thing they did. Mean at least half of it.
Skip the small talk — what would it take to get you on a picture this year?
Lean in: "So. Tell me everything you know that I don't."

fine: {title} is fine. Genuinely. I'm suspicious too.
{title}: on time, on budget. I've bought a lottery ticket.
warn: {title} is... {cast} is directing their own scenes now. Nobody asked them to.
{title} is one rainy day from being a documentary about itself.
bad: {title} needs a decision or a priest.
{title}: the good news is the footage is beautiful. That's also the bill.
